idiom_name: named per-type functions plus C11 _Generic selection over function names
implementation_notes: C has no user-defined operators and no templates, so neither half of the idiom exists: the operator family becomes a family of named functions per type (vec3_eq, vec3_less, money_add) and the only type-generic carrier is a macro using C11 _Generic, which selects a function name from the controlling expression's type (the mechanism <tgmath.h> uses for cos/sinf/cosl). The classic form is justified only in this macro shape: the selection must choose the function name and the call must sit outside the _Generic, because unselected branches are still type-checked. The pragmatic alternative is a naming convention plus comparator callbacks for qsort/bsearch, not an emulation of operator syntax.
alternative: Explicit named functions per type with a consistent prefix (money_eq, money_less, money_add) together with C11 _Generic macros over those names, and qsort/bsearch comparator callbacks where the standard library needs an ordering - C gives user types no way to participate in == or <.
pitfalls: Unselected _Generic branches are still type-checked, so selecting over whole call expressions (_Generic(x, money: money_eq(x, y))) usually fails to compile; select function names and place the call outside.
Every type needs its own function set, and naming drift (money_eq versus eq_money) destroys the uniform vocabulary the macro is supposed to provide.

Macros are not namespaced and bypass type diagnostics: a mismatched _Generic branch is reported at the macro expansion site, and a missing default association makes unlisted types a hard compile error.
